sections.h2: Which offices handle property tax for a Russell County house?
sections.html:
Four offices touch a Russell County tax bill. The PVA, reachable at (270) 343-4395, decides what each parcel is worth. The sheriff, at (270) 343-2191, collects payment. The clerk, at (270) 343-2125, inherits whatever is still open once the sheriff's season ends. The county attorney, at (270) 343-2121, sends the warning letters that precede the clerk's sale.

The fiscal court's own description of the PVA calls the office's valuations the basis of the bills that pay for local services. In plain terms, a complaint about the number goes to the PVA, and a question about where to send the check goes to the sheriff.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Russell County itself?
sections.html:
Russell County is a lake-and-ridge county in south central Kentucky. Lawmakers formed it on December 14, 1825 from pieces of Adair, Cumberland and Wayne counties. It spans 283 square miles, about 29 of them water. Terrain runs from Dickerson Ridge in the far north, at 1,140 feet, down to 530 feet along the Cumberland River. Jamestown holds the courthouse and Russell Springs is larger, at 2,715 people in 2020 against 1,867.

The county runs on Central time, while Casey, Pulaski and Wayne counties along its eastern line use Eastern time. Keep that in mind when you line up a closing with an out-of-county buyer or title office. The Cumberland Parkway crosses Russell Springs toward Columbia and Somerset, and US 127 links the town to the lake area and Tennessee.

  • Wolf Creek Dam, near the county's southern edge, backs up the Cumberland River into Lake Cumberland. Impoundment came in 1952, and the shoreline measures about 1,255 miles.
  • The Army Corps of Engineers began drawing the lake down in 2007 over seepage worries. A new wall inside the dam was done by early 2013, and normal levels returned in spring 2014.
  • Normal summer pool is about 723 feet above sea level, with the tree line near 725.
  • Voters approved alcohol sales on January 19, 2016, by 3,833 to 3,423.
  • Jamestown and Russell Springs got a fiber network in 2015 that made them among the first gigabit internet communities in Kentucky.

Russell Springs grew from a resort built around a mineral spring and was incorporated in 1936. Jamestown was incorporated in 1826 and takes its name from a local landowner, James Wooldridge. If your home is near the water, expect questions about the drawdown history. The county lists a surveyor among its elected offices, which helps when a shoreline boundary is unclear.

sections.h2: What do the numbers say about housing in Russell County?
sections.html:
Housing here is inexpensive and plentiful. The 2020 census counted 10,088 housing units in the county and 26.0 percent of them were empty. Builders pulled just 5 permits in 2025, so new construction is not crowding your listing. About 22.6 percent of residents are 65 or older, and the average trip to work takes 19.8 minutes.

A median value near $163,200 means a Russell County sale rarely turns on a large tax bill, but a stack of unpaid years on an inherited house can still swamp the equity.

sections.h2: Why do buyers look at Russell County?
sections.html:
Mostly for the water. Lake Cumberland, which Wolf Creek Dam created, ranks fourth among the 383 lakes managed by the Army Corps of Engineers for visitor hours, and more than 1,500 houseboats sit on it. Two state parks, Lake Cumberland State Resort Park and General Burnside Island State Park, sit on its shores. The Wolf Creek National Fish Hatchery operates just below the dam inside Russell County.

  • The median age was 43.8 at the 2020 census, and 71.8 percent of occupied homes were owner-occupied.
  • About 29.4 percent of households were one person living alone.
  • Russell County ended 2025 with 18,608 residents, so the market is small and a pricing mistake shows quickly.

Present the house to those buyers with a clean tax record, a current bill in hand and a clear answer on any unpaid years.

sections.h2: When does Russell County tax come due, and what do late payers owe?
sections.html:
KRS 134.015 sets one statewide calendar. Pay in full by November 1 for a 2 percent discount. Through December 31 the printed amount is due. January adds 5 percent, and 10 percent applies from February 1 onward.

Per the clerk's page, bills are mailed in October and the sheriff keeps taking payments through April 15 of the next year. The statute makes the tax a personal debt of whoever owned the property on January 1, so the sales contract should say who reimburses whom.

sections.h2: What happens to an unpaid Russell County bill after April 15?
sections.html:
The sheriff hands the bill to the clerk as a certificate of delinquency, and a lien is recorded on the parcel. That lien stays on the land through a change of owner. The clerk's page promises a tax sale before the end of August, with notice in the newspaper and on the clerk's site. Registered private buyers may purchase the certificate and then pursue the owner.

  • The clerk warns that amounts on the delinquent list shift each month, so call for a current payoff.
  • The Department of Revenue says 1 percent monthly interest runs on the certificate, with clerk and attorney commissions added.
  • A buyer's title search will turn up the lien, so clear it before you close.

sections.h2: How do I contest a Russell County valuation?
sections.html: Start with the PVA: state law wants an informal conference first, and you can ask for it by phone. If that fails, file a written petition with the clerk by the workday after the roll inspection ends. Bring evidence such as listings, building costs or loan papers. The appeal does not stop collection, so pay on your own claimed value in the meantime.

sections.h2: Does Russell County have a homestead exemption?
sections.html:
Yes, for owners 65 and over and for those classified as totally disabled. The Department of Revenue set the deduction at $49,100 for assessment years 2025 and 2026, so a Russell County home assessed at $175,000 is taxed as if it were $125,900. About 22.6 percent of county residents are 65 or older, which makes this the exemption most local owners will ask about.

The PVA takes the application. Disability claimants must show a federal or retirement-system classification and generally renew yearly. Ask the PVA what the figure is for the current assessment year, since the state revises it.

sections.h2: How is tax handled when a Russell County house sells?
sections.html:
Closing agents usually pull the current bill and any delinquent payoff, so request both early. A bill still open before April 15 sits with the sheriff, and after that date the clerk wants it along with extra charges.

Seasonal cabins, inherited homes and houses that fell several years behind deserve a written payoff from the clerk before you advertise them. A buyer who finds a lien in the title search will want it removed or will back out.

faqs.q: Where does a Russell County tax payment go?
faqs.a: To the sheriff's office, at (270) 343-2191, through April 15 of the year after the bill. After that, unpaid bills sit with the county clerk at (270) 343-2125.

faqs.q: What does a late Russell County payment cost?
faqs.a: Five percent in January and ten percent from February 1, under KRS 134.015. Once the clerk holds the bill, 1 percent monthly interest plus clerk and county attorney fees are added.

faqs.q: Will a Russell County tax lien follow a house into a sale?
faqs.a: Yes. KRS 134.015 keeps the lien on the parcel until the tax is paid or the 11-year limit in KRS 134.420 runs out, whoever owns it. A title search flags it.

faqs.q: What month does the Russell County clerk hold the tax sale?
faqs.a: Before the end of August. Newspaper and website notices go out ahead of it, and the clerk's office can confirm the date at (270) 343-2125.

faqs.q: Is the Russell County homestead exemption automatic once I turn 65?
faqs.a: No. Take proof of your age or disability status to the PVA and apply. The 2025 and 2026 amount was $49,100, and most disability claims renew every year.
